description: A doctoral research seminar on current themes in theoretical computer science: convex hierarchies, spectral graph theory, hardness of approximation, average-case complexity, lower bounds, algebraic and geometric methods, and quantum computation. Students read and critique recent papers, test claims on small instances in the maths lab and write a research proposal.
modelledOn: Arora and Barak, Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach
Nielsen and Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information
outcomes: Formulate relaxations of combinatorial problems as linear and semidefinite programs and analyse their rounding and integrality gaps.
Use eigenvalue methods to bound expansion, mixing and cut quality in graphs.
Read a hardness-of-approximation or average-case reduction and reproduce its key gap-preserving step.
Prove and compare lower bounds in communication and query models using rank, fooling-set, polynomial and information arguments.
Analyse small quantum circuits and algorithms and relate quantum complexity classes to classical ones.
Critique a recent paper, state an open problem precisely and write a research proposal with a feasible first result.

units.title: Semidefinite programming hierarchies
topics: Linear and semidefinite programming: duality, feasibility and the ellipsoid method; integrality gaps
Random-hyperplane rounding for MAX-CUT and the 0.878 approximation guarantee
The sum-of-squares hierarchy: levels, moment matrices and pseudo-expectations
Sum-of-squares proofs and the Positivstellensatz; degree and size trade-offs
Applications and limits: planted clique, sparse principal components and sum-of-squares lower bounds

units.title: Spectral methods and expansion
topics: The graph Laplacian: eigenvalues, eigenvectors and the Rayleigh quotient
Cheeger's inequality and spectral partitioning
Expander graphs, the expander mixing lemma and Ramanujan graphs
Random walks: mixing time, conductance and hitting times
Higher-order spectral methods: small-set expansion and spectral clustering of networks

units.title: Hardness of approximation
topics: Gap problems and gap-preserving reductions; approximation classes
The PCP theorem: statement, proof overview via gap amplification and what it says about NP
Label Cover and parallel repetition
Fourier analysis on the Boolean cube, the long code and dictator testing
Optimal inapproximability of 3-variable linear equations and 3-SAT
The Unique Games Conjecture and its consequences for MAX-CUT and vertex cover

units.title: Average-case complexity
topics: Distributional problems, average-case reductions and the class DistNP
Planted clique and computational-statistical gaps
Worst-case to average-case reductions: lattices and learning with errors
The low-degree method and statistical query lower bounds as evidence of hardness
Random constraint satisfaction: satisfiability thresholds and the clustering of solutions

units.title: Communication and query complexity
topics: Deterministic communication complexity: rectangles, fooling sets and the rank bound
Randomised protocols, public versus private coins and the minimax principle
Set disjointness: lower bounds by information complexity and discrepancy
Decision tree complexity, sensitivity, block sensitivity and certificate complexity
The polynomial method and approximate degree
Lifting theorems and streaming lower bounds from communication

units.title: Algebraic and geometric methods
topics: Randomised polynomial identity testing and derandomisation
Algebraic circuits, the VP versus VNP question and matrix multiplication exponents
The polynomial method in combinatorics: cap sets and finite-field Kakeya
Metric embeddings and the random projection lemma; dimension reduction
Error-correcting codes: Reed-Solomon, list decoding and locally decodable codes
Convex geometry: isoperimetry, volume computation and random walks on convex bodies

units.title: Quantum computation and information
topics: Qubits, gates, circuits and measurement; the density matrix formalism
Oracle algorithms: the constant-versus-balanced problem and hidden XOR mask problem
Quantum search and its optimality via the adversary and polynomial methods
The quantum Fourier transform, phase estimation and the factoring algorithm
BQP, QMA and the relation of quantum classes to classical classes
Entanglement, Bell inequalities, the no-cloning theorem and nonlocal games
Quantum error correction, stabiliser codes and fault-tolerance thresholds

units.title: Research practice in theory
topics: Reading a recent paper: extracting the main theorem, technique and what is new
Writing a critique and a proof sketch that a peer can verify
Using computation to test conjectures: small-case search, counterexamples and numerical experiments
Stating an open problem precisely and surveying partial results
Research proposal: question, related work, approach, a feasible first result and risks

schedule.title: Linear and semidefinite relaxations
schedule.exercise: Write the SDP relaxation of MAX-CUT, give its dual, and show by hand that random-hyperplane rounding cuts an edge with probability the angle over pi.

tasks.title: Solve the linear programming relaxation of vertex cover on a 6-vertex graph and show the half-integral solution beats the integer optimum
Round a given SDP solution for MAX-CUT on a 10-vertex graph with 200 random hyperplanes and plot the cut-value distribution against the optimum
Compute the integrality gap of the SDP for MAX-CUT on odd cycles of length 5 to 31 and compare with the approximation guarantee

schedule.title: The sum-of-squares hierarchy
schedule.exercise: Prove that x squared minus 2x plus 1 is a sum of squares, build the level-2 moment matrix for two variables, and read one recent sum-of-squares lower bound paper and summarise its construction.

tasks.title: Express three univariate non-negative polynomials as sums of squares using the symbolic algebra tool and verify by expansion
Build the level-2 moment matrix for a 3-variable Boolean problem and check positive semidefiniteness of a pseudo-expectation candidate
Test whether a degree-4 sum-of-squares certificate exists for a small planted-clique instance and report which constraints fail

schedule.title: Eigenvalues, expansion and mixing
schedule.exercise: Compute the Laplacian spectrum of a path, a cycle and a random 3-regular graph, check Cheeger's inequality on each, and bound the mixing time of a lazy walk.

tasks.title: Compute the Laplacian eigenvalues of a path, a cycle and a complete graph on 8 vertices and relate the second value to connectivity
Partition a 30-vertex graph by the sign of the second eigenvector and compare conductance with the Cheeger bounds
Generate random 3-regular graphs with 50 to 500 vertices, measure the second eigenvalue and compare it with the Ramanujan bound

schedule.title: Gap problems, PCPs and Label Cover
schedule.exercise: Give a gap-preserving reduction from 3-SAT to a gap version of independent set, and explain in a page how gap amplification drives the PCP theorem.

tasks.title: Build the clause-to-triangle graph from a small 3-SAT formula and relate the satisfiable fraction to the largest independent set
Play the Label Cover game on a small bipartite instance with two label sets and find the best strategy by exhaustive search
Simulate parallel repetition of a game with 2 rounds, 3 rounds and 4 rounds, and plot how the best winning probability decays

schedule.title: Fourier analysis, long codes and Unique Games
schedule.exercise: Compute the Fourier expansion of majority on 3 bits, prove a dictator test accepts dictators with probability 1, and describe what the Unique Games Conjecture would imply for vertex cover.

tasks.title: Compute the Fourier coefficients of majority and parity on 3 and 5 bits and verify Parseval's identity numerically
Run a dictator test with 3 queries on all 5-variable Boolean functions and tabulate the acceptance probability of dictators versus others
Reproduce the gap between the best SDP value and the best cut on random instances and compare it with the Unique Games prediction for MAX-CUT

schedule.title: Average-case hardness and random constraints
schedule.exercise: Plant a clique of size k in a random graph on n vertices, find the smallest k at which spectral methods recover it, and compare this with the information-theoretic threshold.

tasks.title: Plant a clique of size 12 in a random graph on 100 vertices and show the clique vertices have higher degree on average
Estimate the satisfiability threshold of random 3-SAT by solving 100 formulas at each clause density from 3.5 to 5.0
Find the clique size at which a spectral algorithm starts recovering a planted clique in graphs of size 200, 400 and 800, and fit the trend

schedule.title: Communication complexity lower bounds
schedule.exercise: Prove the equality function needs n bits deterministically using a fooling set, then give a randomised public-coin protocol with O(log n) bits and its error bound.

tasks.title: Build the communication matrix of equality and greater-than on 4-bit inputs and compute the rank and a fooling set
Simulate the fingerprint protocol for equality with random primes and measure the error rate against the bound over 10,000 trials
Compute the discrepancy of set disjointness on 4 bits by exhaustive rectangle search and compare it with the claimed lower bound

schedule.title: Query complexity and lifting
schedule.exercise: Compute sensitivity and block sensitivity for the OR and a 4-bit function you design, relate them to degree, and state what a lifting theorem transfers.

tasks.title: Compute sensitivity, block sensitivity and certificate complexity for all 3-bit Boolean functions and tabulate the largest gaps
Find the exact and approximate degree of OR and parity on 4 bits with the symbolic tool and compare with their query costs
Build the lifted function of a small gadget on 3-bit inputs, compute its communication matrix rank and compare with the query degree

schedule.title: Polynomials, algebraic circuits and the polynomial method
schedule.exercise: Test whether two determinant expressions are equal with randomised evaluation over a finite field, and explain the cap set bound proof idea in a page.

tasks.title: Test two polynomial expressions for equality at random points over a prime field and estimate the error probability against the degree bound
Compare the cost of the schoolbook and a faster 2 by 2 block matrix product recursion by counting multiplications for sizes 2 to 64
Compute the largest cap set in the 3-dimensional space over three elements by search and compare with the polynomial method bound

schedule.title: Geometry, codes and convex bodies
schedule.exercise: Project a 1000-dimensional point set to 50 dimensions randomly, measure distance distortion, and decode a Reed-Solomon codeword with two errors.

tasks.title: Project 200 points from 1000 to 50 dimensions with a random Gaussian matrix and plot the distribution of pairwise distance ratios
Encode a message with a Reed-Solomon code over a small field, flip two symbols and decode the original by solving the syndrome equations
Estimate the volume of a convex body in 10 dimensions by a random walk and compare against the known value with error bars

schedule.title: Quantum circuits and algorithms
schedule.exercise: Trace a 3-qubit circuit by hand, run the constant-or-balanced algorithm and quantum search on 8 items, and estimate the number of iterations needed.

tasks.title: Apply Hadamard and controlled-NOT matrices to a two-qubit state and print the amplitude vector and measurement probabilities
Simulate quantum search on 16 items and plot success probability against the number of iterations to show the optimum near 3
Simulate phase estimation for a 3-qubit unitary and use the quantum Fourier transform to read out the eigenphase with its error

schedule.title: Quantum complexity, entanglement and error correction
schedule.exercise: Show a CHSH game strategy beating the classical bound of 75 percent, and describe the three-qubit bit-flip code with its syndrome measurements.

tasks.title: Simulate the CHSH game with the best classical strategy and with a shared entangled state, and compare winning rates over 10,000 rounds
Simulate the three-qubit bit-flip code with random single errors and show the syndrome identifies and fixes each one
Draw the known containments between BPP, BQP, NP and PSPACE as a diagram, labelling what is proved and what is conjectured, with a reference for each

schedule.title: Critique, open problems and proposals
schedule.exercise: Present a critique of one recent paper from the course reading list, state one open problem precisely, and submit a two-page proposal with a first result you can test computationally.

tasks.title: Lay out a recent paper's argument as a dependency diagram of lemmas and mark the step you find least convincing
Search all graphs on up to 7 vertices for a counterexample to a conjecture from the reading list and report the search outcome
Run a numerical experiment supporting the first result of your proposal, plot it with error bars and state what it does not prove
